alt.en: A printed book page numbered 112. At the top, the last lines of another carol end with "Sing, oh! &c."; below a short rule comes the heading "I SAW THREE SHIPS." and four verses, beginning "I saw three ships come sailing in On Christmas day, on Christmas day".
alt.es: Página impresa de un libro con el número 112. Arriba, los últimos versos de otro villancico terminan con "Sing, oh! &c."; bajo una raya corta viene el título "I SAW THREE SHIPS." y cuatro estrofas, que empiezan "I saw three ships come sailing in On Christmas day, on Christmas day".

caption.en: The carol on page 112 of William Sandys's Christmas Carols, Ancient and Modern (London, 1833), the book that printed its nine verses, with "Our Saviour Christ and his lady" where we sing "The Virgin Mary and Christ were there".
caption.es: El villancico en la página 112 de Christmas Carols, Ancient and Modern de William Sandys (Londres, 1833), el libro que imprimió sus nueve estrofas, con "Our Saviour Christ and his lady" donde nosotros cantamos "The Virgin Mary and Christ were there".

source: William Sandys, Christmas Carols, Ancient and Modern (London: Richard Beckley, 1833), p. 112, "I Saw Three Ships"

alt.en: The top of a printed page of music, marked 9 in the margin, with the heading "I SAW THREE SHIPS." in outlined capitals and a small pencil cross. Two systems of a tune in one sharp and 3/4 time over a bass line, with the words "I saw three ships come sailing in On Christmas day, on Christmas day" in italic script under the tune; the right edge of the music runs off the page.
alt.es: La parte de arriba de una página impresa de música, con un 9 en el margen, el título "I SAW THREE SHIPS." en mayúsculas perfiladas y una pequeña cruz a lápiz. Dos sistemas de una melodía con un sostenido en la clave y en 3/4 sobre una línea de bajo, con la letra "I saw three ships come sailing in On Christmas day, on Christmas day" en cursiva bajo la melodía; el borde derecho de la música se sale de la página.

caption.en: Tune No. 9, "I Saw Three Ships", in the music at the back of Sandys's book (London, 1833): an earlier form of the tune we sing, in three-four time with dotted rhythms over a bass line.
caption.es: La melodía n.º 9, "I Saw Three Ships", en la música del final del libro de Sandys (Londres, 1833): una forma más antigua de la melodía que cantamos, en 3/4, con ritmos con puntillo sobre una línea de bajo.

source: William Sandys, Christmas Carols, Ancient and Modern (London: Richard Beckley, 1833), music section (unpaginated), air No. 9, "I Saw Three Ships" (top of the page shown)

alt.en: A printed page of music headed "64" and "I saw three Ships." in black-letter type, marked "Briskly" and mf, with four-part harmony on pairs of staves in one sharp and 6/8 time and the words "1. I saw three ships come sail-ing in, On Christ-mas day, on Christ-mas day" between them. Below, a second setting begins, "Or this (in 3 parts)", in one flat; the page number 164 is at the foot.
alt.es: Página impresa de música con el encabezado "64" y "I saw three Ships." en letra gótica, con las indicaciones "Briskly" y mf, armonía a cuatro voces en pares de pentagramas con un sostenido en la clave y en 6/8, y la letra "1. I saw three ships come sail-ing in, On Christ-mas day, on Christ-mas day" entre ellos. Debajo empieza un segundo arreglo, "Or this (in 3 parts)", con un bemol; al pie, el número de página 164.

caption.en: No. 64, "I saw three Ships", on page 164 of an undated printing of Bramley and Stainer's Christmas Carols New and Old: John Stainer's four-part setting, marked "Briskly", first published in October 1878, from which our arrangement is adapted.
caption.es: El n.º 64, "I saw three Ships", en la página 164 de una impresión sin fecha de Christmas Carols New and Old de Bramley y Stainer: el arreglo a cuatro voces de John Stainer, con la indicación "Briskly", publicado por primera vez en octubre de 1878, del que parte nuestro arreglo.

source: H. R. Bramley and John Stainer, Christmas Carols New and Old (London: Novello and Company, Limited; New York: Novello, Ewer and Co., undated), No. 64, p. 164, "I saw three Ships".
